subject: Semicontinuous model to daily rainfall (Blangiardo & Cameletti's book)

messages.author: 3908c89e77a099b3
messages.subject: Semicontinuous model to daily rainfall (Blangiardo & Cameletti's book)
parts:
Hello all,

I am reading the section 8.2 in the Blangiardo and Cameletti book (page 270), and I wonder if there is an errata in page 279. They check the significance of the spatial effects by running the complete range of possible models; in particular, in the model including only the spatial component shared by both responses, they use the following syntax for the formula:

form.oneshared <- alldata ~ -1 + y.intercept + z.intercept + f(y.field, model=spde) + f(z.field, model=spde) 

where y.field is the spatial random effect for the gamma distributed response and z.field is the spatial random effect  for the Bernoulli distributed response (page 275).

I wonder if the code should be as follows:

formula.yz <- alldata ~ -1 + y.intercept + z.intercept + f(y.field, model=spde) + f(zc.field, copy="y.field", fixed=FALSE)

I would like to know if I am wrong in order to be sure that I correctly understood the syntax.

Thank you in advance.

Juan Miguel

Hi,
original off-list response below.
Addition:
Yes, it looks like the book should use the “copy” method, since it specifically says the intent is for there to be a joint effect for the two responses in the model.

Finn

Hi,
Both are valid models, so it depends on which set of models you want (I don’t have the book accessible so can’t check). The first one has two independent fields (presumably one for each likelihood) and the second one has a single field which is just scaled differently for the two likelihoods.  So if they indended a shared effect, the second version should be used. However, in the context of model checking and selection, I can imagine it being useful to run the model with independent components in order to check if it is indeed reasonable to assume that it’s a shared component or not, so in the context you described, one could conceivably run both those models.

Finn

Hi all,

A comment to the first Finn's response below:
--------
 Hi Finn,

Thank you for your response!. Yes, it would be reasonable to run a model with independent components in that context, but my doubt is that they refer to that model as a model with only one shared spatial component, and my thinking is that it does not match with the model syntax they use. So, would there be an errata in the syntax?. I literally cite from the book:

"Also, we can fit a model with only one spatial component which is shared by both responses, i.e., we take out the u_i term in Eq. (8.6):"
form.oneshared <- alldata ~ -1 + y.intercept + z.intercept + f(y.field, model=spde) + f(z.field, model=spde)

page 273
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Eq. 8.6:

logit(pi_i) = b_0 + beta_1*sp_i + u_i

where sp_i is the spatial effect shared with the gamma-distributed response

Thank you

Juan Miguel
